chapters.title: Chapter 3: How Policy Flows Into Asset Prices

lessons.title: Gold, Real Estate, and Your FD: The Wider Ripple

body.text: Most Indian households never buy a government bond or trade the rupee, but almost all of them own fixed deposits, gold or property. RBI decisions reach all three: they set what your FD pays, change how attractive gold is compared with interest-bearing assets, and decide how much a family can afford to borrow for a home.

children.text: This final lesson of Chapter 3 moves from financial markets to the three assets Indian families care about most. The same forces you have studied, policy rates, inflation, liquidity and the rupee, show up here in forms you can see in your own bank statement and property search.
Fixed Deposits: The Slowest Link in the Chain

FD rates follow the repo rate, but with a lag. Banks cut deposit rates only after loan rates fall, and raise them only when they need to attract deposits. After the RBI cut the repo rate by 125 basis points in 2025, SBI lowered its FD rates in steps. Here is where they stood from 15 December 2025.

children.text: The Number That Matters: Your Real, Post-Tax Return

markDefs.definition: The return on an investment after subtracting inflation. It shows whether your money is actually growing in purchasing power.

children.text: An FD's headline rate is not what you earn. Interest is taxed at your income tax slab rate, and inflation eats the rest. The
real return
is what tells you whether your savings are really growing.

body.caption: A simple approximation, ignoring cess and surcharge

body.title: Is Your FD Beating Inflation?
body.prompt: You invest in an SBI 1-year FD at 6.25% and pay tax at the 30% slab. CPI inflation for August 2026 was 4.82%. What is your approximate real post-tax return, in percent? Enter a negative number if you are losing purchasing power, rounded to two decimal places.
body.explanation: Post-tax return = 6.25% × (1 − 0.30) = 4.375%. Real return = 4.375% − 4.82% = about -0.45%. You are losing purchasing power, even though your FD balance grows. This is why inflation matters so much to the MPC: when inflation rises faster than deposit rates, savers in higher tax brackets quietly get poorer.

body.text: Rate cycles change the maths quickly. With SBI Research expecting the RBI to hike by 25 basis points in October 2026 and again in December, FD rates could rise in the months ahead. Locking all your savings into a long FD just before a hiking cycle means missing out on higher rates later. Many savers split money across several maturities, a strategy called laddering, so part of it renews at new rates every year.

body.title: When Should You Lock In a Long FD?
body.question: When is locking into a 5-year FD most attractive for a saver?
options: Just before the RBI is expected to start hiking rates
Near the peak of a hiking cycle, before rates start to fall
Right after a long series of rate cuts, when FD rates are lowest
The timing never matters for FDs
body.explanation: Near the peak of a hiking cycle, deposit rates are high and likely to fall later, so locking in protects your income. Before hikes begin or after a cutting cycle, FD rates are low and likely to rise, so locking in for five years gives up future gains. The same logic explains why gilt funds tend to do well after rate peaks: falling yields raise bond prices.

children.text: Gold: The Asset That Pays No Interest

markDefs.definition: The return you give up by choosing one investment over another. For gold, it is the interest you could have earned on a bond or deposit instead.

children.text: Gold pays no coupon and no dividend. Its return comes only from price changes. That makes interest rates its biggest competitor: when real interest rates are high, holding gold means giving up a lot of safe income. This cost is called the
opportunity cost
of holding gold.

columns.label: Pushes gold up
points: Falling real interest rates, especially in the US
Geopolitical crises and fear in markets

columns.label: Pushes gold down
points: Rising real interest rates and hawkish central banks

body.title: How Far Has Gold Fallen From Its Peak?
body.prompt: Gold hit a record $5,597.23 an ounce on 29 January 2026 and was at $4,263.19 on 15 September 2026. What is the percentage fall? Enter a negative number, rounded to one decimal place.
body.explanation: ($4,263.19 − $5,597.23) ÷ $5,597.23 × 100 = -23.83%. The fall came as US Fed Chair Kevin Warsh signalled possible rate hikes and the dollar strengthened, raising the opportunity cost of holding gold. Gold's link to interest rates works in both directions.

children.text: Why Indian Gold Prices Move Differently

Indians buy gold in rupees, so the domestic price depends on two things: the international dollar price and the rupee exchange rate. When the rupee weakens, Indian gold gets more expensive even if global gold is flat. That cushioned Indian buyers in 2026: the rupee's slide to record lows offset part of the fall in dollar gold prices.

body.latex: \text{Price per 10 g in ₹} \approx \dfrac{\text{Price per ounce in \$} \times \text{₹ per \$}}{31.1035} \times 10
body.caption: One troy ounce is 31.1035 grams. Actual retail prices are higher because of import duty, GST and local premiums.

children.text: At $4,263.19 an ounce and ₹95.6 per dollar, that works out to about ₹1,31,034 per 10 grams before duties and taxes. Retail 24-carat gold was quoted at about ₹15,317 a gram, or roughly ₹1.53 lakh per 10 grams, on 15 September 2026. Most of the difference is tax: on 13 May 2026, as the rupee slid towards record lows, the government raised the effective import duty on gold from 6% to 15% to curb imports and protect forex reserves. Add 15% duty and 3% GST to ₹1,31,034 and you get about ₹1,55,210, close to the retail price.

body.text: The duty hike is a reminder that the rupee is defended with more than just RBI dollar sales. India imported $84 billion of gold and silver in FY26, about 10.8% of its merchandise imports. Making gold costlier to import reduces dollar demand, which supports the rupee, but it also raises what Indian families pay for gold.

children.text: Real Estate: Where Rates Meet the Family Budget
Property is the most rate-sensitive household asset because most homes are bought with loans. Rates reach real estate through three channels:
Buyer affordability:
higher home loan rates raise EMIs and shrink the loan a family qualifies for.
Developer costs:
builders borrow to buy land and construct, so higher rates squeeze their margins and slow new launches.
Relative returns:
residential rents in big Indian cities typically yield only a few percent a year, so when FD and bond rates rise, owning property to rent out looks less attractive.

body.title: What Two Hikes Do to a Home Loan
body.prompt: A family has a ₹50 lakh, 20-year home loan at 7.9% linked to the repo rate. If the RBI hikes by 50 basis points in total and the loan rate rises to 8.40%, how much does the monthly EMI increase? Round to the nearest rupee.
body.explanation: EMI at 7.90% = ₹41,511. EMI at 8.40% = ₹43,075. Increase = ₹1,564 a month, or about ₹18,766 a year. In practice many banks extend the tenure instead of raising the EMI, which keeps the monthly payment the same but adds more total interest. Either way, the hikes SBI Research expects would reverse part of the relief from the 2025 cuts.

body.title: Rental Yield vs an FD
body.prompt: You buy a ₹1 crore flat in a big city and rent it out for ₹25,000 a month. What is the gross annual rental yield, in percent?
body.explanation: Annual rent = ₹25,000 × 12 = ₹3,00,000. Yield = ₹3,00,000 ÷ ₹1,00,00,000 × 100 = 3.0%, before maintenance, property tax and vacancy. An SBI 2-year FD pays 6.40%. Property investors are betting on price appreciation to make up the gap, which is why rising interest rates, which slow price growth, hurt property investment demand.

children.text: What the 2026 Data Shows

Housing demand softened through 2026 as the West Asia conflict, high prices and uncertainty weighed on buyers. Anarock reported a 7% fall in sales across the top cities in January to March 2026, and another 6% fall in April to June 2026, to 90,715 units across seven cities. Yet average prices still rose 7% from a year earlier.

body.caption: Housing Sales, April to June 2026 vs a Year Earlier (Anarock)

body.text: Falling sales with rising prices can look contradictory. It usually means developers are holding prices while fewer buyers can afford them, often because launches have shifted towards costlier homes. If rates rise further in late 2026, the pressure on affordability, especially for first-time buyers taking large loans, would grow.

body.title: Go Deeper: Why Small Savings Rates Barely Move

children.text: In theory, small savings rates are linked to G-Sec yields of similar maturity, with a small spread, and reset every quarter. In practice, the government has often kept them unchanged for long stretches, even when bond yields and bank deposit rates moved. As of July to September 2026, rates had been unchanged for nine consecutive quarters.

This matters for monetary policy. When the RBI cuts, banks lose deposits to schemes like PPF and SCSS that still pay higher rates, which makes banks slower to cut deposit and lending rates. Sticky small savings rates are one reason rate cuts take time to reach borrowers in India.

body.title: Allocating a Retirement Corpus
body.scenario: Your uncle, aged 61, has just retired with ₹40 lakh. It is September 2026. SCSS pays 8.2%, SBI's 5-year senior citizen FD pays 7.05%, gold has fallen about 24% from its January record, and SBI Research expects two RBI rate hikes by December. He wants steady income, and a friend suggests putting it all in gold "because it is cheap now".
body.prompt: How should your uncle think about splitting his money between SCSS, FDs and gold?
body.modelAnswer: His priority is reliable income, not speculation. SCSS at 8.2% is the strongest fit for a large part of the corpus: it is government-backed and pays quarterly interest, but it has an investment ceiling, so check the current limit. For the rest, a ladder of senior citizen FDs across one to five years makes sense: with hikes expected, putting everything into 5-year FDs now would lock out higher rates later, while a ladder renews part of the money each year. Gold can play a small diversifying role, perhaps 5% to 10% through a gold ETF rather than jewellery, but it pays no income and has just shown it can fall about 24% in eight months. "Cheap now" is not a plan; gold could fall further if US rates keep rising. Finally, he should check deposit insurance limits of ₹5 lakh per bank and spread FDs across banks, and account for tax on interest at his slab rate.
